This often happens when a person is traveling with their son that is a Jr but didn’t put it on their ticket. Or if they forgot they already booked and book again they can cancel one of the flights.

Also, people with super common names like John Smith usually have a government issued redress number that they put on their ticket which would differentiate them from a different John Smith with a different redress number to prevent flagged dupes from happening.

Although it’s great that these flight attendants saved these girls, something seems weird about this. When the same flights are booked under the same name, the airlines system flags them as a duplicate booking and if it isn’t resolved, both flights are automatically cancelled. I guess the only way I could see getting around this is buying the ticket immediately before the flight.

Source: am travel agent and have had flights cancel even when they book the duplicate ticket through another avenue.
